name: Park Hyatt Tokyo
name_ja: パーク ハイアット 東京
about: Park Hyatt Tokyo occupies the top floors of the Shinjuku Park Tower in the Nishi-Shinjuku high-rise district. It is known internationally as a filming location for the 2003 film Lost in Translation. The hotel closed for an 18-month renovation and reopened on December 9, 2025, with all 171 rooms and suites renewed. Guests can use the upper-floor restaurants and bar, which look out over the city.
price: Rooms from about 120,000 yen per night (varies by date)
parking: Paid parking on site (self-parking about 4,800 yen per night)

name: Aman Tokyo
about: Aman Tokyo occupies the top floors of the Otemachi Tower, a short walk from Tokyo Station and the Imperial Palace Gardens. The interior uses natural wood, stone and washi paper in a modern Japanese style. The hotel has suites, a spa with a 30-metre pool and several restaurants. Otemachi Station connects directly to the tower.
price: Rooms from about US$1,700 to US$2,500 per night (varies by date)
station: Otemachi Station (Marunouchi, Tozai, Chiyoda, Hanzomon, Mita Lines)
car: Possible, but public transport is easier in central Tokyo

name: The Peninsula Tokyo
name_ja: ザ・ペニンシュラ東京
about: The Peninsula Tokyo stands opposite the Imperial Palace Gardens and next to Hibiya Park, between the Yurakucho and Ginza districts. It is the Tokyo property of the Hong Kong-based Peninsula group. An underground passage links the hotel to Hibiya Station. Ginza and Yurakucho stations are each about a 3-minute walk.
price: Rooms from about US$900 per night (varies by date)
station: Hibiya Station (Hibiya, Chiyoda, Mita Lines), Exit A7
parking: Valet parking on site (about 6,000 yen per night)

name: Imperial Hotel Tokyo
about: The Imperial Hotel opened in 1890 and has long served as a guesthouse for foreign visitors near the Imperial Palace. Its 1923 main building was designed by Frank Lloyd Wright; that building was later demolished, and its central entrance is preserved at the Meiji Mura museum in Inuyama. The hotel faces Hibiya Park. It is part of a redevelopment plan for the area, so check the official site for any closed facilities.
price: Rooms from about US$460 per night (varies by date)
parking: Paid parking on site (covered self-parking about 12,000 yen per day)

name: HOSHINOYA Tokyo
about: HOSHINOYA Tokyo is a high-rise ryokan in the Otemachi business district, built by Hoshino Resorts on the idea of a Japanese inn in a city. Each floor works as a private ryokan with six rooms and a connected lounge. Guests take off their shoes at the entrance and stay in tatami-style rooms. The hotel stands in front of Otemachi Station.
price: Rooms from about US$400 to US$800 per night (varies by date)
station: Otemachi Station (Marunouchi, Tozai, Chiyoda, Hanzomon, Mita Lines)
parking: Paid parking on site (about 5,500 yen per night)
car: Possible, but public transport is easier

name: The Okura Tokyo
about: The Okura Tokyo is the rebuilt version of Hotel Okura Tokyo, a landmark that opened in 1962 and was rebuilt in 2019 with a North Wing and a South Wing. The interiors keep features of the original lobby, such as the lantern-style lights, in a modern design. It is near the Toranomon Hills area and the US Embassy. Toranomon Hills Station is about a 5-minute walk.
station: Toranomon Hills Station (Hibiya Line), Exit A2
car: Possible, but public transport is easier

name: Hotel Gracery Shinjuku
name_ja: ホテルグレイスリー新宿
about: Hotel Gracery Shinjuku is in the Shinjuku Toho Building in Kabukicho. It is known for a large Godzilla head on the 8th-floor terrace, visible from the street. It offers Godzilla-themed rooms, including Godzilla View rooms and a Godzilla Room with a large claw coming through the wall. Reception is open 24 hours, and the 8th floor has a lounge.
station: Seibu-Shinjuku Station (Seibu Shinjuku Line); JR Shinjuku Station is about 5 minutes
parking: Paid parking nearby (the hotel brochure refers to the Shinjuku Toho Building basement)
car: Possible, but public transport is easier

name: TRUNK(HOTEL) CAT STREET
name_ja: トランク(ホテル) キャットストリート
about: TRUNK(HOTEL) CAT STREET is a small hotel on Cat Street, the pedestrian road that links Shibuya and Harajuku. It is run by the Japanese company Trunk, which presents social and environmental themes through its hotel and shop. The location suits visitors who want to walk between Shibuya, Harajuku and Omotesando. It is about 5 minutes from Shibuya Station and 8 minutes from Meiji-jingumae (Harajuku) Station.
price: Rooms from about US$600 per night (varies by date)
car: Possible, but public transport is easier

name: Hotel Ryumeikan Tokyo
about: Hotel Ryumeikan Tokyo is a business-style hotel on the Yaesu side of Tokyo Station, about 3 minutes on foot from the Yaesu North Exit. It has single, double, semi-double and suite rooms, including non-smoking and wheelchair-accessible rooms. Reception is open 24 hours, and staff speak Japanese and English. The location suits travellers using the Shinkansen and other JR lines.
closed: Open daily until 20 May 2027; the whole hotel closes 21 May to 16 July 2027
station: Tokyo Station (JR lines), Yaesu North Exit
car: Possible, but public transport is easier

name: The Millennials Shibuya
name_ja: ザ・ミレニアルズ渋谷
about: The Millennials Shibuya is a capsule-style hotel in the Jinnan area near Shibuya Station. Its sleeping pods have adjustable beds that can fold into a sofa, and the building has a shared lounge. Check-in starts at 3 PM and check-out is at 10 AM, with front desk hours from 7:30 to 1:00 the next day. It is a short walk from Shibuya Crossing.
station: Shibuya Station (JR, Ginza, Hanzomon, Fukutoshin Lines and others)

name: Toyosu Market
about: Toyosu Market is Tokyo's main wholesale market for fish, fruit and vegetables. It opened on October 11, 2018, replacing the Tsukiji wholesale market. Visitors can watch the tuna auction from the observation corridors, or apply in advance for a spot on the tuna auction observation deck. The complex has many restaurants and the Uogashi Yokocho area, with shops selling ingredients, dried goods and kitchen knives. A rooftop garden has views of Rainbow Bridge.
hours: 5:00-17:00 (hours vary by floor, shop and facility; tuna auction viewing about 5:30-6:30)
closed: Sundays, public holidays and most Wednesdays; check the market calendar
car: Possible, but public transport is easier

name: Ichiran Shibuya
about: Ichiran is a tonkotsu (pork bone) ramen chain from Fukuoka. At this Shibuya shop, diners sit in individual booths and order on a form that sets the noodle firmness, broth richness, spice level and other options. The classic tonkotsu ramen costs 1,180 yen, and extra noodles are 210 yen. The shop is open 24 hours. A second Ichiran, Shibuya Spain-zaka, is a different shop with a different number.
price: Ramen from 1,180 yen; extra noodles 210 yen
station: Shibuya Station (JR, Ginza, Hanzomon, Fukutoshin Lines and others)

name: Ameyoko (Ameya-Yokocho)
about: Ameyoko is a shopping street of about 500 metres under and beside the JR tracks between Ueno and Okachimachi stations. It grew out of a black market after World War II, and the name is short for Ameya Yokocho, meaning candy-seller alley. Several hundred shops and stalls sell fresh seafood, dried food, sweets, clothing, cosmetics and souvenirs. Many stalls also sell street food that can be eaten while walking.
closed: Open daily (some shops close on certain days; many close on Wednesdays or around New Year)
price: Free to walk; snacks from about 300 yen
station: Ueno Station (JR Lines), Shinobazu Exit / Okachimachi Station (JR Lines), North Exit
car: Possible, but public transport is easier

name: Gyukatsu Motomura Shibuya
name_ja: 牛かつもと村 渋谷店
about: Gyukatsu Motomura serves gyukatsu, thin-breaded beef cutlets fried briefly and left rare in the centre. Diners cook each slice for a few seconds on a small hot stone at the table, to their preference. Meals come as a set with rice, miso soup and side dishes, and dipping sauces such as wasabi and soy sauce are provided. The shop is in a basement and does not take reservations.
address: B1F Ohno Building No. 2, 3-18-10 Shibuya, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo 150-0002
station: Shibuya Station (JR Yamanote Line), East Exit

name: AFURI Ebisu
about: AFURI is a ramen shop that began near Mount Afuri in Kanagawa. Its signature bowl is yuzu shio ramen, a light salt-based broth flavoured with fresh yuzu citrus juice from Kochi. The Ebisu shop is about a 3-minute walk from JR Ebisu Station. It is cashless, and diners buy a meal ticket at a machine before lining up. The shop may close early when the broth is sold out.
hours: 11:00-5:00 (next day); closes when broth sells out

name: Fuunji
about: Fuunji is a well-known tsukemen (dipping noodle) shop near the south side of Shinjuku Station. The thick noodles come cold with a rich fish and pork broth for dipping, and a small amount of soup is added at the end. The shop is small, does not take reservations, and has a line at lunch.
address: Hokuto Dai-ichi Building, 2-14-3 Yoyogi, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo 151-0053
hours: 11:00-15:00, 17:00-21:00; closes early when the broth runs out
station: Shinjuku Station (JR Lines, Odakyu Line, Keio Line, Marunouchi Line and others), south side

name: Tonkatsu Maisen Aoyama Main Store
name_ja: とんかつ まい泉 青山本店
about: Maisen's Aoyama main store serves tonkatsu, breaded and deep-fried pork cutlet, in a building where the dining hall was once the changing room of a pre-war public bathhouse. The menu includes pork loin and fillet cutlets, often served as a set with rice, miso soup, shredded cabbage and pickles. Maisen also sells katsu sandwiches. It is a short walk from Omotesando Station.
price: Lunch about 1,500 yen; dinner about 4,000 yen
car: Possible, but public transport is easier

name: Harmonica Yokocho
about: Harmonica Yokocho is a network of narrow covered lanes just north of Kichijoji Station. It began as a postwar flea market, and the name refers to its resemblance to the reeds of a harmonica. By day there are clothing stores, a fishmonger and a traditional sweets maker. In the evening, small standing bars and eateries open, mostly for after-work drinks and food. Each shop sets its own hours.
price: Free to walk; meals and drinks about 1,000-3,000 yen
station: Kichijoji Station (JR Chuo Line, Keio Inokashira Line), North Exit
